ns2:course.label: Documenting Inequality
ns2:course.description: Exploration of how economic and social inequality affects the lives of children and minors in the U.S.--especially in minority communities--through the study of documentary film, photography and other kinds of socially conscious art. Students will watch and critique documentaries made by artists and filmmakers in the areas of Education, Housing, and Law Enforcement; go behind the scenes at the Krannert Art Museum to investigate the museum's documentary holdings; and make their own documentary projects. Final projects will be exhibited in the Krannert Art Museum at the end of the semester. Part of the Grand Challenge Learning Inequality & Cultural Understanding pathway.
ns2:course.sectionRegistrationNotes: Restricted to students with Freshman or Sophomore class standing.
ns2:course.sectionDegreeAttributes: Grand Challenge-Inequality, Literature and the Arts, and US Minority Culture(s) course.
ns2:course.classScheduleInformation: This course is intended for first and second year students.
